stories.headline: Putting Christ’s Character into the Workplace
stories.summary: Christians can reflect Jesus through their work habits, business decisions, and how they treat colleagues, turning daily tasks into ministry. This approach makes the workplace a venue for living out the gospel.

stories.headline: Pastoring Across Sovereignty Divides
stories.summary: The author argues that believers’ assurance rests not on personal effort but on Christ’s completed work and God’s promises, urging pastors to guide congregants with differing views on divine sovereignty. Effective ministry, then, hinges on grounding hope in the finished work of Christ.

stories.headline: vLLM Dissects High‑Throughput LLM Inference
stories.summary: A deep‑dive explains how vLLM achieves massive token‑per‑second rates by parallelizing model execution and optimizing memory handling, setting a new benchmark for real‑time AI services. The article details the system’s architecture and performance trade‑offs.

stories.headline: OpenAI Expands Free Access to GPT‑5.6 Luna
stories.summary: OpenAI rolls out performance upgrades to its GPT‑5.6 model and opens the Luna variant to all users at no cost, aiming to boost chat capabilities while gathering broader feedback. The move signals a push to democratize the latest language‑model advances.

stories.headline: U.N. Warns of Mass Atrocities as Drone Strikes Ravage El‑Obeid
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands in Sudan’s El‑Obeid endure relentless drone attacks, severe water shortages, cholera, and widespread sexual violence, prompting the United Nations to issue urgent warnings of escalating atrocities. The humanitarian crisis is deepening amid limited aid access.

stories.headline: We’re Living in an Age Dominated by Lies
stories.summary: The author contends that every historical period has featured deception, but today’s “post‑truth” climate amplifies falsehoods to unprecedented levels, challenging our sense of reality. This surge of misinformation makes discerning truth increasingly difficult.

stories.headline: Finding Gospel Comfort in Parenting’s Painful Transitions
stories.summary: While helping his son move far away, the writer wrestles with how God can redeem the inevitable hurts of parenting, seeking hope in the gospel’s promise amid loss. The piece reflects on divine redemption in everyday family struggles.

stories.headline: OpenAI’s $300 Doughnut‑Shaped Smart Speaker Unveiled
stories.summary: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that OpenAI’s new circular speaker, priced over $300, integrates advanced voice models for continuous, human‑like interaction, aiming to become a daily household assistant. The device is positioned as a companion that learns from everyday use.

stories.headline: Meta Hit with $567 Million Child‑Safety Fine, Totaling $942 Million
stories.summary: A court ordered Meta to pay a record $567 million penalty for child‑safety violations, adding to a prior $375 million sanction and bringing the total fine to $942 million. The ruling marks the largest financial judgment against a social‑media platform for harming minors.

stories.headline: New Mexico Judges Impose $567 Million Penalty on Meta for Youth Harm
stories.summary: A New Mexico court ruled that Meta must pay $567 million for damaging children’s mental health, joining earlier fines to total $942 million, marking the largest child‑safety judgment against a social platform. The decision underscores growing legal pressure on tech firms over user wellbeing.

stories.headline: New Orleans pilots AI-driven 911 triage system
stories.summary: The city is trialing Carbyne’s artificial‑intelligence platform that routes emergency calls without human dispatchers. Officials hope faster, data‑rich triage will improve response times and outcomes.

stories.headline: Thai high‑school shooting leaves at least six dead
stories.summary: A student opened fire at a secondary school in Thailand, killing six people. Police have not yet determined a motive and the investigation continues.

stories.headline: AMD buys Taalas to embed AI models in silicon for faster inference
stories.summary: The chipmaker announced the acquisition of Taalas, a firm specializing in etching neural networks directly onto hardware. The move aims to boost on‑chip AI performance for data‑center workloads.

stories.headline: Study finds humans overlook one‑third of AI‑generated threats in game tests
stories.summary: Across 40,000 simulated game runs, participants failed to flag about 33% of malicious commands issued by AI agents. Researchers warn that reliance on human oversight may be insufficient for safe AI deployment.

stories.headline: Pride vs. Pain: Why arrogance remains a hidden danger for believers
stories.summary: The article argues that Christian teachings condemn pride, yet many underestimate its corrosive effects. It cites historical voices warning that pride fuels deceit and hypocrisy.

stories.headline: OpenAI files aggressive 28‑page motion to toss Apple lawsuit
stories.summary: In a terse filing, OpenAI contends Apple’s complaint lacks any claim of misappropriation. The company seeks a swift dismissal of the case.

stories.headline: Trump issues executive orders to curb birth‑tourism and tighten citizenship rules
stories.summary: The orders aim to block foreign nationals from obtaining U.S. citizenship for their children through travel. They also broaden the categories of people deemed ineligible for birthright citizenship.

stories.headline: Economic pressure pushes more parents to financially support adult children
stories.summary: Surveys show a majority of Americans believe today’s young adults face tougher financial odds than previous generations. Many parents are extending help into adulthood, even at a cost to their own finances.

stories.headline: Audit challenges IBM’s claim of quantum advantage on iron‑sulfur chemistry
stories.summary: A new review questions the validity of IBM’s SQD/QSCI benchmark results, suggesting classical methods may still outperform the quantum approach. The critique reignites debate over practical quantum chemistry breakthroughs.

stories.headline: Ceuta still houses thousands of migrants after border surge, 100 deaths reported
stories.summary: The Spanish enclave’s leader says over 78,000 migrants crossed from Morocco, resulting in about 100 fatalities. Many remain stranded in the city as authorities grapple with the humanitarian fallout.

stories.headline: Blue Island Melds 80s Pop, Rock, and R&B in a Fresh Sonic Expansion
stories.summary: The artist reunites with Dahi to craft velvety tracks steeped in 1980s influences. The partnership pushes the singer’s repertoire into new melodic territory.

stories.headline: Verbolgen’s Third Release Channels Bleak Traditional Black Metal
stories.summary: The cross‑continental duo draws on the grim, emotive roots of classic black metal for their latest record. The album blends that darkness with renewed creative vigor.

stories.headline: Datasette 1.0a38 Patches Critical SQL Injection Vulnerability
stories.summary: The new pre‑release addresses a flaw that could let attackers bypass permissions on databases serving both public and private tables. Administrators are urged to upgrade to protect sensitive data.

stories.headline: Framework Reveals Data Breach Exploiting Metabase Zero‑Day
stories.summary: The hardware company disclosed that attackers leveraged an unpatched Metabase vulnerability to access internal data. Community discussion on Hacker News highlights the incident’s impact and response.

stories.headline: In Lieu Delivers Dreamy Dub‑Infused Beats on Mood Hut Debut
stories.summary: The Texas producer’s inaugural Mood Hut release showcases dub‑style rhythms layered with delicate percussion. The result is a hypnotic, sheen‑filled soundscape.

stories.headline: Wildfire Tragedies Prompt Firefighters to Question Policies and Priorities
stories.summary: Recent deaths and near‑misses have strained an already stressed firefighting workforce. The crisis is sparking debate over safety protocols and resource allocation during a severe fire season.

stories.headline: iOS Shortcut Puts App Preferences One Tap Away from Control Center
stories.summary: A user‑crafted Shortcut lets iPhone users jump directly from Control Center to an app’s Settings page. The trick simplifies accessing preferences that were previously buried in iOS menus.

stories.headline: Frost Fest Mixtape Marries Lo‑Fi Dance Vibes with New York’s Underground Pop
stories.summary: After dropping a polished studio EP, a collective of NY pop innovators released a gritty mixtape. The project features contributions from Kuru, Blaketheman1000, and Gabrielle Turton, among others.

stories.headline: Trump Rejects Claims of U.S. Weapon Shortage, Vows to Pursue Leakers
stories.summary: The former president dismissed reports that America has exhausted hard‑to‑make arms, labeling them misinformation. He warned that those leaking such information are being tracked.

stories.headline: Troy Hunt Invites Nepalese Government to Join Have I Been Pwned
stories.summary: Security expert Troy Hunt announced that Nepal’s authorities can now use his breach‑notification service. The move aims to improve national cybersecurity awareness.

stories.headline: Jharkhand Youth Rally Over Jobs Sparks New Protest Wave
stories.summary: A fresh movement led by young people in Jharkhand is demanding transparent recruitment and more employment opportunities. The campaign follows the recent CJP protests in Delhi and is rapidly gaining momentum.

stories.headline: Judge Orders Meta to Fork Out $567 Million for Youth Mental‑Health Programs
stories.summary: A federal court ruled that Instagram and Facebook must allocate the majority of the sum to treatment services for minors. The decision aims to mitigate the platforms' impact on children's mental‑well‑being.

stories.headline: Phone Mistakes Jogging for Theft, Triggers False Alarm
stories.summary: A user discovered their smartphone's motion sensor flagged a run as someone snatching the device and fleeing. The odd behavior sparked discussion on sensor accuracy and app handling of activity data.

stories.headline: ProvenMetal Promises Domestic PCB Delivery in Days, Not Weeks
stories.summary: The YC‑backed startup claims to turn design files into assembled circuit boards within a few days, aiming to revive U.S. manufacturing share. It positions itself against Chinese dominance that now controls the majority of the global PCB market.

stories.headline: GitHub Reports Degraded Performance for Actions and Pages Services
stories.summary: The status page confirms intermittent availability issues affecting CI workflows and static site hosting. Users are advised to monitor updates as the platform works to restore full functionality.

stories.headline: Taiwan’s President Conducts Midnight Evacuation Drill Amid Invasion Prep
stories.summary: President William Lai participated in an emergency evacuation exercise as part of broader military simulations against a possible Chinese attack. The drill underscores heightened security concerns on the island.

stories.headline: Challies Releases ‘A La Carte’ Issue Featuring Theology, Humor, and Life Reflections
stories.summary: The August 7 edition covers topics from biblical interpretation to personal anecdotes, including a piece on the ‘mark of the beast’ and marital conflict tools. It continues the publication’s tradition of diverse, thought‑provoking content.

stories.headline: African Nations Split on Backing FIFA Chief Infantino
stories.summary: While CAF has not issued an official position, individual African football powers are voicing divergent opinions on Infantino’s leadership. The debate reflects broader concerns about governance and the sport’s future on the continent.

stories.headline: Datasette 0.65.3 Released with Back‑ported SQL Injection Fix
stories.summary: The latest version incorporates a security patch originally introduced in the 1.0a38 build, strengthening protection against injection attacks. Developers are encouraged to upgrade to maintain safe data publishing.

stories.headline: Simon Willison Shares Insights on Why He Blogs Technically
stories.summary: In an interview with Cynthia Dunlop, Willison explains his motivations for starting and continuing his technical blog. He also reflects on the value of writing for personal growth and community engagement.

stories.headline: Australian crew lands in darkness to rescue patient from Antarctica base
stories.summary: The Australian aviation team touched down at McMurdo Station in total darkness with temperatures plunging to -43 °C. They successfully evacuated a sick patient, marking a rare midwinter rescue on the continent.

stories.headline: BMW says no in‑car advertising despite expanding screens
stories.summary: BMW confirmed it will not sell ad space on its vehicle displays, even as it rolls out larger screens like a 31‑inch rear‑seat theater. Executives argue that existing radio ads are intrusive enough and the brand wants to keep the cabin experience ad‑free.

stories.headline: Trump pushes new birthright citizenship limits as Iran‑Oman pact looms
stories.summary: The former president issued orders aimed at tightening birthright citizenship rules while diplomatic talks between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz progressed. Meanwhile, Trump faces mounting pressure to secure a breakthrough in negotiations with Iran.

stories.headline: BMW drivers outraged as Spider‑Man ads appear on dashboard screens
stories.summary: Owners of newer BMW models reported unsolicited Spider‑Man: Brand New Day promotions popping up on their digital instrument clusters. The campaign sparked a backlash on social media, with some drivers claiming they were billed up to $160,000 for the feature.

stories.headline: Engineered chewing gum could target HPV and other microbes
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a bio‑engineered gum that releases antiviral agents capable of neutralizing HPV and similar pathogens. Early lab tests suggest the gum could become a convenient, everyday preventive tool against microbial infections.

stories.headline: South Korea’s lunar orbiter captures Moon before and after SpaceX debris impact
stories.summary: Korea’s space agency released images showing the lunar surface moments before a fragment of a SpaceX rocket struck it. The photos provide a rare visual record of human‑made debris colliding with the Moon.

stories.headline: Iran’s parliament eyes toll and bans on US/Israeli ships in Hormuz, US rejects
stories.summary: Lawmakers in Tehran are considering a plan to prohibit vessels from the United States, Israel and other hostile nations from transiting the Strait of Hormuz and to levy fees on others. The proposal has been dismissed by the Trump administration as untenable.

stories.headline: Israeli settler charged with reckless manslaughter in killing of West Bank filmmaker
stories.summary: Yinon Levy faces a reckless manslaughter charge for the July 2025 shooting of Odeh Hathaleen, who starred in an Oscar‑winning West Bank film. The case highlights ongoing tensions over settler violence and cultural representation.

stories.headline: UEFA says boycott could proceed despite FA pulling support for Infantino
stories.summary: UEFA maintains that a planned football boycott remains possible even after the English FA withdrew its backing of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. The governing body argues that the meeting’s outcome does not alter the broader dissent among European associations.

stories.headline: Quiz teases 'step back from visibility' trend and asks about TMZ origins
stories.summary: A new NPR quiz challenges listeners to identify who is choosing to reduce their public profile, while also testing knowledge of the acronym TMZ. The interactive segment aims to blend pop‑culture trivia with current media discussions.
